bill.title: Imposes higher percentage of interest and other civil penalties on certain employers or their workers compensation insurance carriers for non-payment of a bill for medical care or supplies

posted_text:
🛠️ NY A11714 — NY Employers Could Face Higher Penalties for Delayed Medical Bills

New York is increasing the financial consequences for employers or their worker’s compensation insurance carriers who fail to pay medical bills promptly.

Specifically, the bill adds a $50 fee per award made by the board, plus interest accruing at 1.5% per month starting 45 days after the bill is rendered.

If a pattern of non-payment is identified, interest rates can increase to between 3% and 5% per month.

Furthermore, egregious or repeated violations could trigger a civil penalty of up to 25% of the unpaid amount.

Sept. 16, 2026: Referred to Labor.

🔗 Read the full bill: https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/bills/2025/A11714
